# Technical safety requirements

All the technical safety requirements of [WP-S-02](../WP-S-02-technical-safety-requirements.md) on one page: the parameters of the safety envelope and what each bounds, every requirement with its component, ASIL and time, the safety mechanisms they belong to, their allocation to hardware and software, and how each is verified. They refine the [functional safety concept](../../02-concept/fsc/README.md) through the mechanisms of the [technical safety concept](../tsc/README.md). Everything here is generated by `tsr.py` from `tsr.yaml`; CI fails if it is stale. Everything is a draft by Claude (I0) until it is reviewed.

1. [What these requirements are](#1-what-these-requirements-are)

3. [Requirements](#3-requirements)

## 1. What these requirements are

Technical safety requirements (TSRs) refined from the functional safety requirements of [WP-C-04](../../02-concept/WP-C-04-functional-safety-concept.md), one level down: what each safety mechanism of [WP-S-03](../WP-S-03-technical-safety-concept-architecture.md) must do, on which component, in hardware or software, within which time of [WP-S-04](../WP-S-04-timing-ftti-budget.md), and how it is verified.

Needed at gate G2 ([WP-M-00](../../01-management/WP-M-00-work-product-register.md)).

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: tsr-summary (assurance/03-system/tsr/tsr.py) -->

45 technical safety requirements refine the 34 rated FSRs through the 19 safety mechanisms of WP-S-03, on 10 components; 12 of them fall to suppliers under the DIA. 21 carry a detection or reaction budget from WP-S-04. 13 parameters set the envelope, 3 of them decided by the lead; no requirement waits on an open decision.

<!-- END GENERATED: tsr-summary -->

The model is kept in `tsr/tsr.yaml`; `tsr/tsr.py` checks it against the technical safety concept, the timing budget and the decision register, and writes the tables and Figure 4-1. It refuses a model in which a mechanism has no requirement, an FSR a mechanism implements is refined by none of its requirements, a requirement sits on a component its mechanism neither runs on nor uses, or a requirement claims a budget its mechanism does not have.

**The ASIL of a requirement is derived, not typed.** It is the highest ASIL of the FSRs it refines. On the safety LiDAR and radar, which the lead decided to decompose (DQ-031 A), a requirement refining an ASIL D FSR takes ASIL B(D); a requirement refining an FSR of another ASIL keeps that ASIL, because the decomposition split only the ASIL D detection.

The requirements of components outside the item (drive-by-wire, vehicle state sensing, park brake, doors, monitor supply, remote operations station) are requirements on their suppliers, to be agreed in the development interface agreement (DIA) and met by supplier evidence.

## 2. Envelope parameters

The requirements name their parameters rather than repeating values. A parameter takes its value from the timing model of WP-S-04 (a goal's margin or a mechanism's detection budget), from a decision of the lead, or from the vehicle once it is chosen (DQ-008). No value is measured, and once one is set it is not loosened to make a finding go away.

Two of these set how the vehicle behaves and were decided by the lead on 2026-10-24: the monitor brakes at no more than 3 m/s² when its sensors cannot see the reason, which is also the level of its own stop (P-05, DQ-033 A), and it assumes the vehicle ahead may brake as hard as a car can and that pedestrians may run and cyclists ride fast out of an occlusion (P-06 and P-07, DQ-034 A). The rest follow from WP-S-04 or from the vehicle.

**Autoware has to drive inside these assumptions.** At 50 km/h the monitor keeps 19.5 m to the vehicle ahead. If Autoware follows closer or passes parked cars faster than P-06 and P-07 allow, the monitor will brake for it often; Autoware's planning parameters must therefore be set at or beyond them (OI-2).

**Finding: decomposition does not split the false-alarm requirement.** The safety channel counts a road user seen by either sensor (DQ-031 A), so a false detection by either sensor can make the monitor brake hard, the hazard of SG-03 (ASIL C). Each sensor therefore carries an ASIL C requirement on its false detections (TSR-09.04, TSR-09.05) alongside its ASIL B(D) detection requirement, Braking hard only when both sensors agree would have lowered the false-alarm requirement but weakened the detection the collision goal rests on. The lead decided that each sensor is developed to ASIL C for false detections as well as to ASIL B(D) for detection (DQ-035 A, 2026-10-24); WP-S-03 shows both, and `tsr.py` refuses a requirement on a decomposed component whose ASIL WP-S-03 does not show.

## 4. Safety mechanisms: detection, reaction, fallback

Each mechanism with its requirements, the share of its binding FTTI it has to detect a fault and to react (WP-S-04 §4), and the fallback it starts ([WP-C-12](../../02-concept/WP-C-12-fallback-and-minimal-risk-concept.md)). A mechanism without a reaction prevents the hazard by bounding a command or delivering a signal, rather than by detecting a fault.

The safety monitor's requirements are almost all software on an ASIL D controller; its own fault detection is hardware (lockstep, memory protection, watchdog). The hardware-software interface that carries these requirements is specified in [WP-S-05](../WP-S-05-hsi-specification.md), and hardware and software safety requirements are refined from this allocation in the hardware and software work products.

## 6. Verification criteria

Each requirement is verified at system level ([WP-S-08](../WP-S-08-system-integration-test.md), [WP-S-09](../WP-S-09-system-verification.md)); a supplier's requirement first by the supplier's evidence under the DIA. A requirement with a time is passed only by a measurement inside its budget (WP-S-04 §6). A requirement that waits on a decision is verified against the value the decision sets.
